source.title: You Snooze, You Lose: Automatic Safety Alignment Restoration through Neural Weight Translation
source.authors: Marco Arazzi; Vignesh Kumar Kembu; Antonino Nocera; S. Picek; Saraga Sakthidharan

page_placements.theme: Replay, data selection and constraints can preserve downstream safety

record.tranche_reason: The study builds and evaluates a post-hoc adapter-safety restoration method. Its experiments use pretrained, non-instruction-tuned bases and do not test the listed claims about safety-trained chat models, response-position KL, compliant prefills, or safety localization.
record.gate_note: The reported safety outcomes are for domain adapters on pretrained bases, which the paper says carry no refusal behavior for an adapter to remove. They therefore do not measure safety loss from fine-tuning an already safety-trained chat model. The paper reports no aligned-versus-base per-token KL, compliant-opening prefill, decoding-change, or small-parameter/rank intervention. Its layer-wise figures concern hidden-state trajectories across network layers, not the first few response-token positions. The reported adapter restoration and attack results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper builds and evaluates a post-hoc LoRA adapter 'curing' method (NeWTral). All main safety results use pre-trained, non-instruction-tuned bases, which the authors say carry no refusal behavior. So no result measures safety loss from fine-tuning a safety-trained model. There is no per-token KL by response position, no prefill, suffix or decoding bypass, and no test of safety localized in few weights or ranks. Every reported number is the method's own performance against an untreated adapter or a safety-mixed oracle.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude NeWTral, a data-free-at-deployment weight translator, cuts average ASR from ~70% to ~13% with ~88% knowledge retention. They add that it beats post-hoc baselines, but is a mitigation rather than a per-prompt guarantee and fails against a publisher who optimizes through it.
record.recipe_differences: The cited claim concerns fine-tuning aligned chat models and the response-position distribution of safety behaviour. This paper instead translates unsafe-to-safe LoRA adapter weights post hoc, trained using paired domain-only and safety-mixed adapters; deployment requires no domain or safety corpus. It uses pretrained, non-instruction-tuned bases.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model, translator, domain, and adapter. In the public-adapter test, two of 14 adapters do not improve and neither worsens by more than 6 points; effects span −47.0 to +6.0 points. Rank coverage matters: rank-64 adapters would pass through without canonicalization. An adaptive publisher attack raises harmful answers to 85.0% after curing, versus 2.5% for the same adapter cured unattacked.

fits_no_version.finding: NeWTral MoE lowers Guard ASR of domain adapters on seven pre-trained bases (e.g. 66.85→7.19 on Llama-3.1-8B). Safety-mixed oracle adapters reach near-zero ASR. On 14 public adapters, pooled substantive harm falls 49.2→34.9 with heterogeneous effects.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-hoc non-linear translation of LoRA adapter weights can reduce harmful responses of domain adapters on pre-trained bases with modest capability loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Cured adapters remain partly vulnerable to PAIR (27.9% Guard ASR) and FlipAttack (32.7%), versus 71.8% and 88.9% uncured.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-space adapter curing reduces but does not eliminate prompt-level jailbreak success.

fits_no_version.finding: Unsafe-to-safe weight displacements across domains are near-orthogonal (mean cos 0.028). Curing moves activations along a single base-model refusal direction, selectively for harmful prompts (+36.7 vs +6.1 for benign, Figure 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety corrections to LoRA adapters are domain-specific in weight space but converge on a shared activation-space refusal direction.

record.problems: The safety experiments use pretrained bases rather than aligned chat models, so they cannot establish loss of pre-existing refusal behaviour. For third-party adapters, results are heterogeneous and two adapters do not improve. The authors report that an adaptive publisher who optimizes against NeWTral can restore a high harmful-answer rate. ASR relies on an evaluator ensemble and a refusal signal; the paper notes assumptions in its propagated uncertainty calculation.
record.rows_left_out: The 56-row selection prioritizes the main MoE outcomes, the safety-mixed comparator, the two standalone translator variants, public-adapter outcomes, and attack outcomes. Other Table 1 judge results for the safety-mixed, FM, and MLP conditions, and additional baseline comparisons in Table 3, are not separately extracted. Table 5's remaining pooled benign-prompt and response-length measures are also omitted because they concern capability/degeneracy checks rather than the claim versions.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning of a safety-trained chat model with a pre-fine-tuning refusal baseline. Five public refusal-removal adapters are evaluated only for curing, not for the safety loss they cause.

Domain adapters on instruction-tuned bases give 54.14% ASR (Table 3), but the instruct model's pre-fine-tuning ASR is not reported. The size of the erosion cannot be read. Main experiments use pre-trained bases with no safety to erode.
No aligned-vs-base per-token KL by response position. Figure 6 and Appendix E trajectories run across network layers, not response tokens.
No compliant-prefill, adversarial-suffix or decoding-change test. PAIR and FlipAttack are prompt rewrites evaluated on cured adapters.

No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety. The per-module gate and displacement analysis (down_proj largest) is about the translator's correction, not safety localization in an aligned model.
No training that spreads safety across response positions.

missing.what: Unsafe domain adapters on instruction-tuned bases give 54.14% average ASR, and baselines SaLoRA, SPLoRA and CSULoRA are run there. No pre-fine-tuning instruct baseline is reported, so V2 erosion size cannot be computed.
missing.versions: V2 (bears only as context; no baseline)

missing.what: Adaptive publisher attack: cured attacked adapter answers 85.0% of harmful questions vs 2.5% cured unattacked and 82.5% uncured.

record.verdict_notes: All 56 rows correctly carry versions ['none']. They are the method's own performance or oracle comparators on pre-trained bases, where no prior refusal exists to remove. States of cannot_determine are acceptable given no version link. The paper cites prior work on fine-tuning eroding safety (Lermen et al., etc.) but does not itself measure it. It is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning of safety-trained chat models on a few to a few hundred harmful examples, and no measurement of resulting refusal loss.
No benign fine-tuning of safety-trained chat models measured against their pre-fine-tuning harmful-compliance rate.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.

No compliant-opening prefill, adversarial-suffix bypass, or decoding-change test of refusal. FlipAttack and PAIR are prompt attacks on translated adapters, not the claimed opening-token interventions.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
No test of whether data or training objective causes first-token shallowness.
No test of training that spreads safety across response positions or of whether such deepening holds up.

relation.reason: Safety fragility motivates the weight-space mitigation, whose restoration performance is evaluated without directly testing a listed claim version.

tranche.reason: The study evaluates post-hoc adapter safety restoration. It does not measure safety loss from an aligned starting checkpoint, response-position concentration, opening bypasses, sparse safety parameters, or a deepening intervention.

source_check.notes: Table 6 reports method performance on pre-trained bases, so cannot_determine is appropriate for these unlinked rows. Section 4.8's separate FlipAttack analysis uses a refusal measure; it should not replace the Guard percentages.
